title: Complementary ideals in a semisimple Lie algebra
statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field] and let $L$ be a finite-dimensional $F$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Assume that $L$ is semisimple in the sense of [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], namely every solvable Lie ideal of $L$ is zero. For every Lie ideal $I\subseteq L$, there exists a Lie ideal $J\subseteq L$ such that $I\cap J=0$ and $I+J=L$ (sum and intersection of subspaces).

source.place: §22c, printed p.475 (PDF p.487), final paragraph under The Casimir operator: the kernel ideal has a complementary ideal, obtained using the Killing form; characteristic-zero and finite-dimensional hypotheses at the start of §22c.

mathlib_match.how: Specializes in one line: choose J = I.killingCompl and use LieIdeal.isCompl_killingCompl I (Killing.lean:142-143); IsCompl says exactly intersection zero and sum top. The semisimple predicate is HasTrivialRadical F L, precisely as recorded by def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra via hasTrivialRadical_iff_no_solvable_ideals (Semisimple/Basic.lean:67-69). The required IsKilling F L is inferred by LieAlgebra.HasTrivialRadical.instIsKilling (CartanCriterion.lean:258-259, hypotheses at 49 and 198); a field and Module.Finite supply IsDomain, Module.Free and IsNoetherian. Thus no extra hypothesis or comparison theorem is needed. The theorem gives an actual ideal, not just a vector-space complement.
